summary.verdict: 2/10 at 400 — the round-11 BLOCKER is closed and the four items I was asked to verify are genuinely good, but a strict re-read of the rubric text against fresh counterexamples demotes five systems. Blocker cleared: `bun test` at HEAD is 427 pass / 1 todo / 0 fail (428 tests, 20 files) and `bunx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 — the SlabSlice `y:`-vs-`elevation:` typo, the 1-arg test.todo and the RED tsc are all fixed, and the gate's non-finite guard means the floor/foundation-slab scenarios no longer pass vacuously. VERIFIED GOOD (not taken on faith — 17 throwaway bun scripts, since deleted): electrical Phase 0 connectivity is real — I built 15 plans the harness has never seen (rectangles at 0/7/17/30/37/45/63/90/123deg, an opening-saturated panel wall, an L, an L rotated 23deg, an oblique trapezoid, two disconnected wings, degenerate zero-length and curved walls) and `unreachableDevices` returns 0 on every one; foundation Y-junction clustering is fixed (3 walls at one point, 0 violations at 0deg and 27deg); the SDC-D rebar-vs-anchor-bolt nudge is fixed (26 bolts vs 48 verticals, min plan distance 101.6 mm, 0 violations); per-bay floor blocking is fixed (`bayLen = rows[i+1]-rows[i]-t`, floor-framing.ts:580-608 — plain 5x8, 12x12+wall, L+hole, narrow and tiny slabs all 0 violations, closing the round-10/11 38-172 mm overrun); the perf gate is real and passes; `buildPlanSet` costs only 1.9-3.7 ms p50 so plans are not a perf risk. NEW FINDINGS. (1) wall-layers is OUTSIDE the interpenetration gate and clashes on the plainest possible plan: a 6x4 rectangle yields 20 layer-involved clashes — 8.70 mm of through-wall drywall buried inside the butting wall's plates and studs, drywall-x-drywall at every inside corner, and exterior corners left OPEN (cladding ends at x=6.078 while the neighbour stops at x=6.000). `runInsets` (wall-layers.ts:139-140) only insets the layer when the other wall is longer, so at equal-length corners neither retreats. (2) Assembly thickness double-counts the finish: a drawn 4.49 in wall becomes 5.49 in finished with the boards floating 12.55 mm off the studs, contradicting `data/wall-assemblies.json`'s own `interior.totalThicknessIn: 4.5` (= 0.5 drywall + 3.5 framing + 0.5 drywall). `emitStack` starts at `offset = wall.thickness/2` instead of stacking inward from the drawn face. (3) Those 20 layer members produce 0 takeoff rows and 0 cut-list lines (they carry no `size`), and takeoff.ts has no `cladding`/`wrb` handling at all — no siding, housewrap or trim line item exists on any sheet. (4) Foundation `mark()` uses `Math.max(e[which], sign)` (foundation.ts:151), so an end that is both a through-corner and an interior tee takes the extend branch and drives a wing footing 0.4 m into the main wall's runs (4 violations, survives a 33deg rotation). (5) `obliqueK`'s `cross < 0.3` cutoff (foundation.ts:184-192) leaves 15deg and 5deg corners completely unmitered (2 violations each) — both a gap and a clash. (6) A 4-way X-junction clashes (2 violations). (7) The commonest topology in a real plan fails: an exterior wall drawn as TWO segments with a partition teeing at the joint gives a 203 mm footing double-pour at the splice (`w_s1{-1.00,1.00}` extends past x=6 while `w_s2{0.00,...}` stays flush) — the literal thing foundation-350 forbids. (8) Sistered joists (`sisterCross = wallCross + t`, floor-framing.ts:450) are guarded only against `trimmerLines` (:454), never against blocking or the adjacent common, so they collide at every parallel-bearing-wall position I tried. (9) Non-axis-aligned slabs: 86 clashes @45.9 mm (10deg), 133 @30.8 mm (30deg), 115 @19.8 mm (45deg), with no warning flags. (10) Roof: flat 36 @15 mm, gambrel 212 @59 mm, mansard 104 @45 mm, dutch 72-100 @42 mm, gable at pitch <=12deg puts collar ties and ceiling joists up to 153 mm inside the ridge, and outlookers pierce rafters on 16x12 and 24x18 gables @34 mm. (11) Plans silently truncate: a 60-wall house drops 11 of 93 takeoff rows (`rows.slice(0, 2*maxLines)`, plan-set.ts) and prints only 4 flags (`flags.slice(0,4)`), with no 'continued' marker; and `planSheet` reads yaw from `rotation[1]` and tilt from `rotation[2]` while ignoring `rotation[0]` (plan-set.ts:177-179), so on a yawed roof the outlookers draw 5.82deg off axis and 45 mm short. REFUTED / STILL OPEN from round-11 (re-verified at HEAD, unchanged): oblique wall corners double-stack bottom, top AND cap plates at 20/30/45/60deg (3 violations each) and cap plates at 120/135deg — the (1+|cos|)/sin fix still has not been ported out of foundation.ts; CMU oblique corners double-stack blocks at 45/60/120deg (12 violations each, 90deg clean); the stair-hole sweep still fails 34 of 101 positions (trimmer x common); joists still pierce rims on rotated slabs; plumbing and HVAC still route on WORLD X/Z — on a 17/30/45deg plan only 2 of ~27 horizontal runs are parallel to ANY wall (25-27 are parallel to world X/Z), pipes sit up to 1.50 m and ducts 1.56 m from any wall. SCORING NOTE: wall-framing, roof, foundation, plumbing and hvac drop 350->300 not because anything regressed but because I am applying the rubric text literally where rounds 10-11 did not — 'not doubled-up naive overlap' / 'gambrel + dutch + mansard + flat framed' / 'no double-pours at corners' / 'Manhattan ALONG WALLS' are each falsified by a numeric counterexample above. takeoff drops 400->350 on the 'every member' clause of the cut-list criterion. Priority for round 15: put wall-layers inside the interpenetration gate and fix the offset/inset math (it is the only defect that fires on an unrotated rectangle, i.e. on the default house); then port the oblique-corner multiplier into wall-framing and cmu; then make the MEP and floor-clipping bases wall-relative instead of world-relative.
